title.justification: The paper primarily investigates whether forward gradient methods can match the performance of backpropagation in neural network training.

extractions.description: This paper explores the use of forward gradients as an alternative to backpropagation for training neural networks. The authors discuss the limitations of backpropagation, such as memory and synchronization requirements, and propose forward gradients as a more efficient and potentially biologically plausible method. They conduct a study on various combinations of gradient targets and guesses using neural network architectures like ResNet-18. The paper suggests that forward gradients, particularly with local gradient guesses, can improve efficiency and scalability, though challenges remain in matching the accuracy of backpropagation.

primary_category.quote: The motivation of Forward Gradient descent is to approximate End-to-End Gradient descent. However, this unbiased gradient approximation generally suffers from high variance.
